messages:
Mia: FYI: seeing ~15% p99 token latency regression on hosted after the new compat routing change. Looks correlated with fallback/compat paths producing much smaller batches.
Sam: Can you paste quick numbers or a profile? sounds like batching fragmentation to me.
Mia: Quick summary from this morning: baseline avg_batch_size=5.1, fallback-path avg_batch_size=2.3. KV cache hit rate basically unchanged. Tokens/sec down and p99 up. Profiling shows an extra kernel-compat validation per request (~1.1ms) and many tiny batches losing amortization.
Leo: Are fallbacks chosen at routing-time or mid-request? If we do per-request validation during execution that could spike kernel selection overhead.
Mia: Routing-time decision. But the runtime still runs a per-request compat check at enqueue/execute boundary which triggers a short sync path.
Anya: Observed many queues where token_budget < 10 leading to frequent flushes. If we instead gate on cumulative tokens (token-budget target) we can avoid tiny batches.
bench-bot: bench: 2026-03-17 03:14 baseline run -> batch_size=5.1 tokens/s=1020 p99=41ms; fallback-path run -> batch_size=2.3 tokens/s=640 p99=50ms
Sam: Two candidate mitigations: 1) merge compat-sets to a single universal execution kernel (safer for batching but may degrade numerical fidelity for some quantized variants), 2) queue policy tweaks (short delay + cumulative token target) to reduce fragmentation.
Mia: Merging kernels worries me for accuracy on certain quantized families. Need prompt-suite evals before enabling broadly.
Leo: I prototyped lazy-family-tagging: router stamps requests with a family tag (attn_v1 / attn_v2). The executor accumulates family mix; if mixed then pick family-common kernel. In dev this reduced per-request checks by ~60% and increased avg batch size.
Anya: Another useful knob is token_budget_target per-queue: e.g., target_tokens=40 or 32. Collect until cumulative_tokens >= target OR delay_ms hit.
Sam: Proposed small canary config (pseudo):
```json
{
  "queue": {
    "delay_ms": 6,
    "target_tokens": 32,
    "compat_merge": "lazy-family",
    "max_delay_ms": 30
  }
}
```
Sam: Keep delay small for canary; zero for latency-SLO tiers.
Mia: Canary with delay_ms=6 showed avg_batch_size -> 3.9 and p99 improved ~9% on mixed traffic vs fallback-only path. Good sign.
bench-bot: bench: 2026-03-17 03:55 canary run -> queue-delay=6,target_tokens=32 => batch_size=3.9 tokens/s=890 p99=46ms (fallback path was 50-52ms)
Anya: Caveat: adding delay adds extra wait for single-shot requests if theres no other traffic. Must gate by customer_tier / SLO label.
Mia: Add emergency rule: if batch_size < 2 and compat_mix_ratio > 0.5 then immediate execute to avoid long wait. Also enforce hard max_delay_ms=30.
Sam: For observability we'll record per-queue: batch_size, compat_mix_ratio, kernel_switch_count, kernel_validation_time, cumulative_tokens_at_flush.
Leo: Quality: run evals on 1k prompt suite comparing family-common kernel vs per-variant kernels. We need <0.5% delta on critical prompts.
Mia: I'll run the eval harness and produce per-prompt deltas and summary metrics. Also capture KVCandidateHit vs effective_cache_hits post-change since merging kernels could change activation lifetimes.
infra-bot: deploy: route-policy-canary v2 rolled to 10% at 1751235000
Sam: Implementation tasks: (1) implement token-budget gating and delay_ms logic in queue, (2) implement lazy-family-tagging + family-common fallback, (3) feature flags by customer_tier/SLO, (4) integration tests for token-budget and compat-mix behaviors.
Mia: I'll own evals and dashboarding. Sam will land feature flags and tests. Leo will run accuracy checks. Anya will monitor queue metrics.
Sam: Will add a hard-rollback: if p99 regressions for latency-SLO customers >5% during canary, auto-disable queue-delay for that tenant.
Mia: Thanks team. Posting updates here as canary runs and evals complete. If we see single-shot regressions we rollback the policy immediately.
bench-bot: scheduled perf sweep at 1751238000
Mia: :thumbsup:
